did: Built the failure accounting the owner asked for: every failure home meets is now one count and one error line, made together by a sealed Failure token, and a new HomeFailures alert sends any count to Slack. The first user is the Jobs mailbox: a handing it refuses, can never take, or holds other bytes for is counted and logged with the mailbox's reason, and a file it can never take is no longer handed again. Beside that, a separate shrink-only ratchet now stops any new silent erasure of a Result, without touching the clippy baseline rule. Of the mailbox pass's other sites, only a kept body that does not read as its name is one event, and that is counted; the sites where a failure persists, and would be counted again every pass or restart, wait on the owner's choice.

calls.title: Make a failure's step a closed list rather than a free string
options: A closed Step table, each step naming its process, started at zero at boot
A free string per call site, as the proposal sketched
calls.why: A series born at its first failure is invisible to increase(), so a step's first failure, and the first after a restart, would never alert; a closed list can start every series at zero.
calls.undo: Swap Step for a string in failure.rs and give HomeFailures an arm for a series' first sample.

calls.title: Count a conflicting mailbox handing as a failure, not only a refusal
options: Count conflict, refused and unfit handings
calls.why: A conflict is final and the file never reaches the routine, the same loss as a refusal.
calls.undo: Drop the Conflict arm's count in mailbox/pass.rs's Handing.

left: The mailbox failures that persist (an open restore ask, a skipped newest file, an unreadable held week, a refused index put) are not counted, since each pass or restart would count them again; the owner chooses a counted-once table or an open-failures gauge (server#1201).
Counting the files the Jobs indexes skip waits on reading them once at keep time (server#1200).
A routine's status still says waiting for a refused or absent take; that is a wording change, not accounting, split out for the owner (server#1199).
The erasure ratchet reads hidden erasures lexically; letting clippy see them with --force-warn needs a policy call on reasoned exceptions (server#1202).
The other high-risk CONSERVE children (#1176 to #1182 and #809) are not started.
